meta.title: One franc per thousand — A citizen-led, humanist and non-partisan initiative
meta.description: Swiss federal popular initiative for the introduction of a micro-tax on electronic transactions.

hero.tagline: A citizen-led, humanist and non-partisan initiative — in service of people

preambule.label: Our conviction
preambule.titre: Why we are carrying this initiative
preambule.sous: A citizen-led, humanist and non-partisan initiative — in service of people
preambule.p1: We, Swiss citizens, carry this initiative without partisan affiliation and without ideological agenda. We carry it because a simple and long-held conviction unites us: systems are made to serve human beings — not the other way around.
preambule.p2: Not everyone suffers in the same way. But everyone shares the same reality: a tax system that levies on those who live and work, and lets pass those who merely grow their wealth. To rebalance this is to give back to each person what is rightfully theirs.
preambule.p3: Rent goes up, health insurance premiums go up, prices go up. Wages stay the same. And taxes take their share before life has even begun. Meanwhile, one hundred trillion francs flow through Switzerland every year in electronic transactions without contributing significantly to the common good. This imbalance is not inevitable. It is the result of a tax system designed in another era, for another economy.
preambule.p4: This is not a question of right or left. It is a question of basic justice. This is not a technical question. It is a human question.
preambule.p5: A levy of one franc per thousand on these transactions is enough to rebalance this disparity. To abolish the direct federal tax that weighs on every salary. To reduce the VAT that hits every daily purchase. To give every household real purchasing power back — without miracles, without debt, without raising social contributions.
preambule.p6: This initiative does not belong to any party. It belongs to every person who believes that a just society is one where the tax system serves people — and not people who serve the system.
preambule.signature: The initiative committee — Swiss citizens of diverse perspectives, united by a shared humanist conviction.

metaphore.label: To understand simply
metaphore.titre: One leaf picked from a thousand.
metaphore.sous: The tree feels nothing. The forest changes everything.
metaphore.p1: Imagine a vast forest. From every tree, one leaf in a thousand is picked. The tree does not notice — by the following season, it has grown back. But with the leaves of every tree in the forest, you can shelter, heat and feed an entire village.
metaphore.p2_before: That is exactly what this initiative proposes: one franc per thousand on electronic transactions.
metaphore.p2_strong: Imperceptible for each person. Decisive for everyone.

chiffres.sous: A citizen-led, humanist and non-partisan initiative — in service of people

identite.label: Our identity
identite.sous: Citizen-led, humanist, non-partisan — three words that are not slogans

items.desc: It does not come from a party, a lobby or a pressure group. It comes from citizens exercising a fundamental constitutional right — to directly propose an amendment to their country's fundamental law.
It stems from a long-held and simple conviction: institutions and tax systems are tools created by humans to serve humans. When they no longer fulfil that role, they must be corrected.

It is not morally neutral — it has clear values. But it owes nothing to any camp. It reduces taxes on labour (what the right demands) and taxes what merely grows wealth (what the left demands). It belongs to everyone.
Behind every number, there is a concrete reality: rent paid, a health insurance premium absorbed, the end of the month made easier. Purchasing power restored. That is why this initiative exists.

objections.label: Frequently asked questions
objections.titre: What opponents say — and the truth
objections.intro: A humanist and non-partisan initiative has a duty to answer every objection honestly.

items.r: Hong Kong, Taiwan and the United Kingdom have taxed transactions for decades. Their financial centres remain among the most dynamic in the world. The real economy is not going anywhere.
The first year is an audit year at a near-zero rate. No tax is abolished before the figures are certified. The initiative is built on prudence.
No. The Tobin tax targeted currencies. This initiative covers all electronic payments at a rate one hundred times lower — making it unprecedented and far more equitable.
Not everyone suffers in the same way. But the relief benefits everyone — and first and foremost those whose purchasing power is most constrained.
It reduces taxes on labour (what the right demands) and taxes what merely grows wealth (what the left demands). It is humanist and non-partisan.

items.q: « The cantons will lose their autonomy. »
items.r: The initiative only affects federal taxes. Each canton remains entirely in control of its own taxation.

regles.titre: Rules to follow for your signature to be valid
regles.sous: An invalid signature is a lost signature. These rules are simple but absolute.

items.titre: Same municipality on the entire sheet
items.desc: All signatories on the same sheet must be registered in the same municipality. Do not mix municipalities.
Last name, first name, date of birth and signature must be written by hand, in ink. No printing, no stamps.

items.titre: Swiss citizens of voting age only
items.desc: Only Swiss nationals aged 18 or over who are registered on the electoral roll of their municipality may sign.
Signing twice — even on two different sheets — invalidates both signatures. One signature per person.
No signature collected before publication in the Federal Gazette is valid. The date appears on each sheet.
Sheets must reach us early enough for us to send them to the municipalities for attestation. Plan ahead.
